newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela CANTV union rejects pay offer,may strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela CANTV union rejects pay offer,may strike.

text.p: Workers at Venezuelan telephone company CANTV rejected Wednesday the company's most recent wage offer and said they may strike.

The latest pay offer "is an insult to our intelligence," Telecommunications union Fetratel president Cruz Hernandez told Reuters. "We'll call a national telecommunications strike if the company continues with this attitude of not increasing wages."

However, Hernandez said any decision to strike would follow union meetings due to begin Monday. In addition, the National Workers Inspector will chair a meeting next Wednesday between labor and management to see if such action can be averted, he added.
The latest offer upped basic salary increases for 1997 to 21 percent from a previous offer of 20 percent, but at the same time reduced 1998 increases from 18 percent to 17 percent.
"If management wants to bring this problem to a head, so be it, we accept the challenge," Hernandez said.
CANTV said the increases, including bonuses, translated into a 37 percent hike in take home pay for 1996 and a 77 percent hike for next year.
"CANTV pays its workers among the three best paid rates in the country," said Miguel Leon, vice president of Human Resources.
